name: The Meridian Compact
description: Vantablack's most expensive production to date at Φ900 million, a neural-feed historical epic in which you experience the 2147 founding negotiations of GLMZ through the eyes of six different characters — corporate founder, city planner, Shelf community organizer, labor negotiator, and two unnamed citizens — whose perspectives overlap and contradict across a single pivotal night. The multi-perspective neural architecture required viewers to purchase all six 'strands' separately, generating massive secondary revenue. Universally praised for its technical achievement and criticized for its politics.
cultural_impact: The phrase 'which strand did you run' became M88 shorthand for asking someone's political perspective, and the leaked director's cut of the organizer strand circulates as one of the most sought-after underground media artifacts of the 2210s.
story_hooks: Ferreira-Obi encoded the complete director's cut of all six strands into a single black-market chip and smuggled it out before Vantablack could seize his assets — someone just found it.
A Spire law firm is hunting down everyone who has seen the leaked organizer strand, claiming it contains proprietary neural-architecture code that constitutes IP theft.

The 'unnamed citizen' strand — the cheapest and least-marketed — contains a 4-second subliminal sequence that no one at Vantablack can explain, and three viewers who noticed it have reported the same recurring dream.
